label: prf:q-dilogarithm-unique
title: Proof of uniqueness of the $q$-dilogarithm
html:
Proof. Proof of uniqueness of the q-dilogarithm

Assume the five-term relation is rigid on H: the only map satisfying it identically is the zero map.

The relation is additive in the evaluation map, so if two q-dilogarithm structures share the pentagon data (\mathrm{mul}, \mathrm{compl}, \mathrm{div}), the difference of their evaluation maps again satisfies it. Rigidity forces that difference to vanish, so the two evaluation maps agree.

Rigidity is the one-dimensionality of the solution space of the level-2 shuffle recursion modulo lower-level primitives, and it is stated as a hypothesis rather than discharged. The conclusion reaches the evaluation map only: the pentagon identity constrains that map and not the level-2 element \mathrm{Li}_2^q itself, so determining the element needs a normalisation the present data does not carry.
